title: Rollback hooks per component: define hook contract, ordering, and rollback-safe boundaries
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Context
Private upgrades are staged across multiple components (control plane, gateway, runtime, observability agents). We need deterministic rollback behavior when:
- a step fails mid-upgrade (e.g., chart install fails, readiness gate times out)
- post-upgrade smoke test fails
- operator triggers manual rollback

Today we can “re-apply previous chart versions”, but we don’t have a contract for per-component rollback behavior (e.g., draining traffic, pausing reconcilers, restoring config/state, ensuring we don’t create split-brain). This ticket defines the hook contract + ordering rules and specifies how upgrade orchestration marks rollback-safe boundaries/checkpoints.

Goal
1) Define a hook interface (pre/post) that components can implement for upgrade and rollback.
2) Define deterministic ordering across components for executing hooks.
3) Define “rollback-safe boundaries” (checkpoints) that the installer/upgrade controller records and uses to decide if rollback is allowed and what rollback plan to run.
4) Provide implementation guidance for Helm-chart-level hooks/jobs + installer integration.

Non-goals
- Building the entire rollback command UX (tracked in ENG-2314 / PR follow-ups).
- Guaranteeing downgrade support across forward-only data migrations (policy in rollback compatibility doc). We *must* integrate with that policy via guardrails.

Definitions
- Component: a unit upgraded/rolled back as a set (e.g., control-plane, gateway, runtime, observability-pack)
- Hook: an optional action invoked by the orchestrator around an upgrade/rollback step
- Checkpoint (rollback-safe boundary): a persisted marker indicating we reached a state where rolling back to a prior version is considered safe under the current compatibility policy (e.g., no forward-only migrations have been applied past the checkpoint).

Proposed design
A) Hook contract
Hooks are invoked by the private installer (or upgrade controller) and may be implemented as:
- Kubernetes Job/Helm hook (preferred for on-prem/VPC consistency)
- Control plane API call (only if it can be executed in air-gapped environments without external dependencies)

Hook interface (logical)
- name: string (e.g., control-plane.preRollback)
- component: enum {control-plane, gateway, runtime, observability}
- phase: enum {preUpgrade, postUpgrade, preRollback, postRollback}
- version_context: {from_version, to_version, target_checkpoint_id}
- timeout_seconds: integer
- retries: integer (default 0; hooks must be idempotent if retries > 0)
- outputs: structured log lines + optional “artifact paths” to include in diagnostics bundle

Execution semantics
- Hooks MUST be:
  - idempotent (safe to run twice)
  - bounded (timeout enforced)
  - side-effect explicit (document what state is changed)
- Hooks MUST NOT:
  - perform schema migrations directly unless explicitly designated as the “migration step” and registered with the rollback policy guardrails
  - depend on external connectivity beyond the cluster (air-gapped requirement)

Exit status mapping
- Success: continue
- Retryable failure: (only if hook declares it) orchestrator retries up to N
- Non-retryable failure: orchestrator stops and moves to rollback plan (if allowed) or enters “Manual intervention required” state

B) Ordering / dependency graph
We will treat components as a directed acyclic graph for ordering. Initial ordering (v1):
- Upgrade order:
  1) control-plane
  2) runtime
  3) gateway
  4) observability agents
- Rollback order (reverse with safety constraints):
  1) gateway (quiesce / drain)
  2) runtime
  3) control-plane
  4) observability agents (best-effort)

Rationale:
- Gateway should be drained/paused first during rollback to avoid routing requests to a mixed-version control-plane/runtime.
- Control-plane rollback should be last among core components to ensure it can coordinate shutdown/health signals where possible.

NOTE: If we introduce region/zone sharded runtime pools later, ordering becomes per-pool; out of scope for v1.

C) Rollback-safe boundaries (checkpoints)
We will introduce explicit checkpoints recorded by the orchestrator as it progresses.
- checkpoint_id: opaque id (e.g., timestamp + upgrade correlation id)
- recorded_at: time
- versions: {control-plane, runtime, gateway, observability}
- migration_state: reference to control-plane “migration metadata” indicating whether any forward-only migrations have been applied

Rules
- A checkpoint is “rollback-safe” only if:
  - all components in scope are healthy at the checkpoint
  - no forward-only migrations have been applied past the prior checkpoint (per rollback policy)
  - backups/snapshots required for rollback have been verified (ENG-2317)

Suggested checkpoint points (v1)
- CP0: pre-upgrade, after prechecks + backup verification succeeds
- CP1: after control-plane upgrade + postUpgrade hook passes + readiness gate passes
- CP2: after runtime upgrade + readiness gate passes
- CP3: after gateway upgrade + smoke test passes
- CP4: after observability agents updated (optional; doesn’t block rollback-safety)

Rollback plan selection
- If failure occurs between CP0 and CP1: rollback to “previous known good” by restoring snapshots and re-applying previous charts (safe)
- If failure occurs after CP1:
  - consult migration metadata; if forward-only migrations applied, rollback may be disallowed (enter Manual intervention required with explicit message and Support playbook link)
  - otherwise rollback to most recent rollback-safe checkpoint

D) Implementation details (Helm + installer)
- Charts expose optional hook Jobs via values:
  - rollbackHooks.enabled=true
  - rollbackHooks.timeoutSeconds
  - rollbackHooks.serviceAccountName (for least privilege)
- Hook jobs should:
  - emit structured logs with correlation id
  - write a small JSON result to stdout (installer captures)
  - be annotated with explicit “hook type” so diagnostics can find them

Installer responsibilities
- Construct plan graph: components + steps + hooks + gates
- Persist checkpoint markers (likely control-plane state endpoint; see control plane version reporting endpoint work)
- Enforce ordering and stop-the-world behavior when needed
- Produce explicit UX:
  - “Rollback allowed: yes/no (reason)”
  - “Rollback target: CPx / version set”

Open questions
1) Where do we persist checkpoints on-prem?
- Proposal: in the control-plane DB (cluster-local) with a simple table keyed by upgrade correlation id; fallback: installer local disk for fully offline “installer-driven” upgrades.

2) How do we avoid hook drift across versions?
- Proposal: hook contracts are versioned alongside chart versions; installer enforces supported hook schema by compatibility matrix (ENG-2315).

3) How do we handle partial rollbacks (e.g., only gateway rollback)?
- v1: no partial rollback; rollback is a coordinated action across the ordered component set.

Acceptance criteria
- Written contract added to the upgrade design docs (Confluence) with:
  - hook phases + semantics + exit codes
  - required properties (idempotency, timeouts)
  - ordering rules
  - checkpoint model and rollback plan selection
- Installer can:
  - register and invoke hooks per component (or no-op if not present)
  - record checkpoints at defined boundaries
  - present “rollback allowed/blocked” with clear reason when blocked by forward-only migrations
- Helm charts can expose at least one real hook implementation (gateway drain/quiesce OR control-plane pause reconcilers) behind feature flag
- SRE review completed on ordering + failure modes
- Security review notes captured for hook RBAC/service accounts

References
- Confluence: Private upgrade framework overview (upgrade phases + invariants)
- Confluence: Rollback policy & downgrade compatibility (forward-only migration guardrails)
- Linear: ENG-2317 (backup primitive), ENG-2320 (helm sequencing), ENG-2321 (upgrade telemetry)

Implementation plan (this ticket)
1) Draft contract + ordering proposal and get sign-off (Ethan, Sean, Connor)
2) Add checkpoint spec + persist location decision
3) Define Helm values + job templates for hooks
4) Stub installer integration points (invoke hook, enforce timeout, capture output)
5) Add “rollback blocked” reasons mapped to policy failures
6) Add minimal e2e test case in harness (hook fails -> rollback plan triggered) (coordinate w/ ENG-2322)
comments: 2025-02-07 (Connor O'Brien): Please make sure the contract explicitly calls out which phases are required vs optional. Release Eng needs deterministic behavior across VPC + on-prem. Also: add exit status mapping (retryable vs non-retryable) so we can keep the orchestration logic simple.

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): Ordering looks right, but I want a hard requirement that gateway preRollback drains traffic and that installer can confirm drain completion (or at least time out + warn). We saw split-brain-ish behavior in staging when gateway stayed live while CP was being reverted.

2025-02-12 (Marcus Lin): Hooks running as Jobs need tight RBAC. Please add guidance: dedicated service account per hook type, no cluster-admin. Also ensure hook logs don’t print secrets (especially if we capture into diagnostics bundles).

2025-02-18 (Devon Price): Drafted hook phases + checkpoint model; pushing for “checkpoint persisted in control-plane DB” as primary. For air-gapped, installer-only persistence is risky because it complicates recovery if the operator moves machines; but we can keep a local copy as a fallback.

2025-02-21 (Michael Nguyen): Migration guardrails need to be part of checkpoint determination. If migration metadata says forward-only applied, rollback must be blocked even if component health is OK. Suggest we store migration state snapshot in checkpoint record to make troubleshooting easier.

2025-02-26 (Kenji Nakamura): Operator UX note: when rollback is blocked, the message must be actionable (what to do next, link to runbook section). Avoid generic “not supported”. Provide exact reason: forward-only migration X applied at time Y.

2025-03-03 (Ethan Park): Marking In Review. Main open item is checkpoint persistence location for on-prem. Leaning CP DB + local fallback. Need final sign-off from SRE + Security on RBAC + artifact collection boundaries.
